findings.description: User-set webhook subscriberUrl is fetched server-side; API v1 create/edit apply no SSRF check and the sync validator skips DNS resolution, so SSRF via v1 URLs or DNS-rebinding reaches the sink.
findings.source: Webhook subscriber config (webhook.subscriberUrl) set by any authenticated user
findings.demotionReason: trpc & API v2 webhook create/edit validate subscriberUrl via validateUrlForSSRFSync (blocks cloud-metadata + literal private IPs on SaaS); API v1 create/edit apply no SSRF check and the sync validator does no DNS resolution (DNS-rebinding gap), so v1-registered or rebinding hosts reach the fetch sink. Corroborated by Layer 4 axios SSRF advisory (CVE-2025-62718).

findings.description: Legacy AES-256-CBC decrypt has no authentication tag: ciphertext is malleable and exposed to padding-oracle/bit-flipping. Used for stored credential secrets; key is latin1-buffered.
findings.source: Encrypted stored credentials/secrets (DB ciphertext) decrypted with the env key
findings.demotionReason: An authenticated AES-256-GCM keyring (packages/lib/crypto/keyring.ts, setAAD+getAuthTag) exists as the correct replacement, but the unauthenticated legacy CBC path remains in production use (known-weak control at high severity).

findings.description: Legacy AES-256-CBC encrypt gives confidentiality without integrity (no MAC); latin1 key encoding mis-buffers non-ASCII key bytes. Protects stored OAuth/app credentials.
findings.source: Plaintext credentials/secrets encrypted with the CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY env key
findings.demotionReason: Authenticated AES-256-GCM keyring (packages/lib/crypto/keyring.ts) is the correct available replacement, but the no-MAC legacy CBC primitive is still used in production (known-weak control at high severity).

findings.description: Attendee is fetched by integer id with no owner/tenant scoping, so any authenticated API-key holder can enumerate other users' attendee PII (name, email, booking). No object-level authz.
findings.source: API v1 path parameter req.query.id (any valid API key holder)
findings.demotionReason: API-key authentication is enforced but object-level authorization is absent: the handler scopes only by id, not by owner/tenant. Authentication is present yet insufficient as the authz control (bypassable for cross-user access) at high severity.

findings.description: Redirect destination is built from the 'return-to' cookie; new URL(value, base) lets an absolute URL override the base, so a controlled cookie yields an off-site redirect (phishing).
findings.source: 'return-to' cookie value (app-managed; read in edge proxy)
findings.demotionReason: Target derives from an app-managed 'return-to' cookie, not a direct request parameter, and exploitation requires controlling that cookie (scope-limited, phishing-only/medium). No same-origin allowlist on new URL() - recommend an allowlist.

findings.description: OAuth authorization-code redirect target comes from body.redirectUri; without validation this would leak the code, but the value is allowlist-checked before use.
findings.source: OAuth authorize request body.redirectUri
findings.demotionReason: redirectUri is validated against the OAuth client's registered redirectUris via isOriginAllowed() before res.redirect, and the endpoint is guarded by NextAuthGuard - a functionally sound allowlist mitigation is on the path.

findings.description: The iframe message handler authorizes on a spoofable data.originator field instead of e.origin, so any frame can invoke interfaceWithParent methods. Methods only reconfigure embed UI.
findings.source: Cross-origin window 'message' event (any frame can postMessage)
findings.demotionReason: The dispatched interfaceWithParent methods only reconfigure the embed UI for the hosting page (the embedder is the intended message sender by design), limiting impact; recommend a strict e.origin allowlist. Scope-limited at medium severity.

findings.description: postMessage uses wildcard targetOrigin '*', so UI control messages are delivered to whatever origin occupies the iframe. Payload carries only non-sensitive embed UI control data.
findings.source: Parent SDK -> iframe control messages (CAL method/arg)
findings.demotionReason: targetOrigin '*' sends only non-sensitive UI control/dimension messages to the embedder (which already controls the host page); no credentials/PII in the payload. A code TODO already acknowledges pinning targetOrigin. Defense-in-depth/low.

findings.description: Parent SDK message listener parses e.data.fullType and fires action-manager callbacks without checking e.origin, so any frame can trigger embed UI action callbacks.
findings.source: Cross-origin window 'message' event in the parent SDK
findings.demotionReason: Actions fired are client-side UI callbacks (link-ready, dimension changes, navigation within the embed) with no privileged or server-side effect; recommend an e.origin allowlist. Scope-limited at medium severity.

findings.description: User bio rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML, but the value passes through the centralized markdownToSafeHTML (sanitize-html) wrapper before injection, neutralizing active markup.
findings.source: User-supplied team/profile bio (team.bio)
findings.demotionReason: The centralized markdownToSafeHTML/sanitize-html sanitizer (mitigation-inventory cat 8 Output Sanitization) is on the dataflow path, and a per-request CSP nonce + strict-dynamic (apps/web/lib/csp.ts) adds defense-in-depth. Functionally sound, medium.

findings.description: An inline script interpolates pageStatus into the DOM, but pageStatus is a fixed server-side status enum, not user-controlled data, so no untrusted value reaches the sink.
findings.source: Server-computed pageStatus enum (not user input)
findings.demotionReason: The interpolated value (pageStatus) is a server-side enum constant, not attacker-controlled input; no untrusted data is on the path. Scope-limited/low; recommend a nonce'd JSON script element for hardening.

findings.description: $executeRawUnsafe is invoked with a server-generated query template plus a separate bound-parameter array (...parameters), so user values are parameterized rather than concatenated.
findings.source: Bulk child event-type update inputs (server-built query + parameters)
findings.demotionReason: Values are passed as bound parameters (...parameters) and the SQL template is server-built, so Prisma parameterization (mitigation-inventory cat 2, 884 files) is on the path and suppresses injection. Impact-rated high but not exploitable as written.

findings.description: child_process calls interpolate paths/commands, but every call-site is a build/CLI/dev script (app-store-cli, sentry, prisma migrate, seed) not reachable from the production request path.
findings.source: App-store CLI argument appDirPath (developer/CI input, build-time)
findings.demotionReason: All command-injection sinks are confined to build/CLI/dev tooling with developer- or CI-controlled arguments, not end-user input, and are absent from the production runtime request flow (deployment/scope-limited). Medium impact if a script were exposed.

findings.description: A DESCRIPTION.md path is built from the app dirName and read with readFileSync; dirName originates from the controlled app-store metadata enum, not raw user input, and runs at static generation.
findings.source: App-store app dirName (controlled metadata from DB)
findings.demotionReason: The path segment (dirName) comes from the curated app-store metadata enum in the DB, not free-text user input, and the read executes at build/static-generation time - no user-supplied '../' reaches the path. Scope-limited/low.

findings.description: User-controlled OAuth state is JSON.parse'd, but JSON.parse in JS/TS only produces plain data (no constructor/gadget execution), so this is not a deserialization-RCE sink.
findings.source: OAuth callback query parameter req.query.state
findings.demotionReason: JSON.parse in JS/TS has no code-execution deserialization gadget (unlike Java/Python); parsed state is consumed as data and the only downstream risk (returnTo redirect) is tracked under Open redirect. Most webhook JSON.parse paths are Zod safeParse-guarded. Low.

findings.description: The only XML-parser sink is the browser DOMParser used client-side for rich-text/clipboard HTML; the browser DOMParser does not resolve external entities, so XXE is not reachable.
findings.source: Pasted/clipboard HTML in the rich-text editor (client-side)
findings.demotionReason: Browser DOMParser does not process external entities (no XXE by spec), the parsing is client-side on the user's own paste, and there is no server-side XML parser with entity expansion on any path. Low.

findings.description: The user-set webhook payloadTemplate is compiled with Handlebars; logic-less Handlebars is sandboxed by default (no code execution / prototype access) and renders only the owner's own event payload.
findings.source: Webhook payloadTemplate (set by the webhook owner)
findings.demotionReason: Handlebars compile() is logic-less and sandboxed by default (no eval/constructor/__proto__ access), no unsafe-eval helper is registered, and the render context is the webhook owner's own event data - no cross-tenant or RCE path. Low.

findings.description: Every 'merge(' match is a Zod schema .merge() (compile/type-level schema composition), not a recursive object merge; no __proto__/deepmerge/_.merge sink consumes user-controlled keys.
findings.source: Zod schema composition (not runtime user object merge)
findings.demotionReason: The matched 'merge(' call-sites are Zod schema .merge() type-level composition, not recursive object merges, and no __proto__ / deepmerge / lodash.merge sink accepts attacker keys - not exploitable for prototype pollution. Low.

findings.description: Math.random()-derived strings are used only as fallback team name/slug when Stripe metadata is missing (not as tokens/secrets), so predictability has no security impact here.
findings.source: generateRandomString() fallback for team name/slug
findings.demotionReason: Verified the value backs only non-security fallback team name/slug (route.ts L71-72), not an auth secret/token; the shared packages/lib/random.ts helper must still use a CSPRNG (crypto.randomBytes) for any security context. Non-security usage/low.

findings.description: Hardcoded-secret matches are dominated by object/property names, Zod schema fields, and process.env reads rather than literal embedded credentials; no real secret value is bound to a source/sink path.
findings.source: Pattern (secret|token|api_key|password)[:=] over source (mostly identifiers, not literals)
findings.sink: csrfToken: z.string()  // schema field name, not an embedded credential
findings.demotionReason: Matches are predominantly property names, Zod schema fields, and process.env reads, not literal credentials; authoritative secret detection is delegated to Layer 2 Semgrep p/secrets and the Layer 1 config audit. No taint dataflow applies. Low.

findings.description: Double-submit CSRF token is validated, but the cookie-vs-submitted comparison uses non-constant-time !==; token timing leakage is not practically exploitable since the attacker supplies the value.
findings.source: Submitted csrfToken vs 'calcom.csrf_token' cookie (double-submit)
findings.demotionReason: The double-submit CSRF token IS validated on state-changing routes (reset-password, cancel, guest-session); the comparison is non-constant-time but CSRF-token timing leakage is not practically exploitable (the attacker already supplies the value). Functionally sound control/low.

findings.description: User-derived data reaching console/logger calls could embed newlines to forge log lines (CWE-117), but impact is limited to log integrity with no RCE or secret exposure.
findings.source: User-derived values/error messages passed to loggers
findings.demotionReason: Impact is limited to log-forging/integrity (no RCE or secret disclosure); most logging is server-side diagnostics through a structured logger that reduces injection impact; recommend newline-sanitizing user-derived log fields. Low.

findings.description: Dynamic RegExp is built from admin/app-configured origin allowlists (escaped, wildcard -> linear .*); the pattern is not attacker-controlled, so catastrophic backtracking is not reachable.
findings.source: CORS/OAuth allowed-origin patterns (admin/client-configured)
findings.sink: new RegExp(wildcardToRegex(pattern))  // input escaped, wildcard -> linear .*
findings.demotionReason: RegExp patterns derive from developer/admin-configured values (OAuth client origins, app urlRegExp metadata) or escaped variable names; wildcardToRegex escapes input then uses linear '.*'. No attacker-controlled catastrophic pattern is on the path. Low.

findings.description: All existsSync/stat sinks are in build-time/CLI/dev tooling (app-store-cli, swagger generation, devin scripts); there is no production request-path check-then-use file race.
findings.source: Local filesystem state in build/CLI tooling
findings.demotionReason: existsSync/stat call-sites are confined to build/CLI/dev tooling and operate on developer/CI filesystem state, not a production request path; the check-then-use is not user-triggerable. Scope-limited/low.

findings.description: MD5 derives an email verification-code secret keyed with a server secret and short TTL; the relevant property (preimage resistance) holds, so MD5 collision weakness does not apply here.
findings.source: Email + server secret + expiry used to derive a verification code secret
findings.demotionReason: MD5 here derives a keyed verification secret (server secret + email + short expiry) where collision resistance is not required and preimage resistance holds; recommend migrating to SHA-256/HMAC. Limited impact at medium severity.

findings.description: HMAC-SHA1 is used to verify inbound Vercel webhook signatures; HMAC-SHA1 remains cryptographically sound (SHA-1 collision weakness does not affect HMAC) and the algorithm is mandated by the provider.
findings.source: Inbound Vercel webhook body + shared webhook secret
findings.demotionReason: HMAC-SHA1 is still cryptographically sound (SHA-1 collisions do not affect HMAC) and the algorithm is dictated by the external Vercel webhook signature spec, so it is not attacker-selectable. Low.

findings.description: Event-type delete is keyed by id, but checkPermissions() enforces owner/team-owner/system-admin authorization before the delete, so cross-user deletion is blocked.
findings.source: API v1 path parameter req.query.id
findings.demotionReason: Object-level authorization is enforced by checkPermissions() (owner/team-owner/system-admin) before the delete - a validated authz mitigation is on the path. Contrasts with the unguarded attendees/[id] read, documenting the v1 authz-parity baseline. Mitigated.
